children: rose 9.20% premarket after second quarter revenue rose 58% to $46.97 billion, ahead of the $44.89 billion consensus. Non-GAAP diluted EPS came in at $7.04 against $4.91 expected, up 203%. GAAP diluted EPS was $6.34.

Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue climbed 89% to $31.8 billion, with AI-optimized servers doubling to $16.4 billion and traditional servers and networking up 122% to $10.5 billion. Storage rose 26% to $4.9 billion. Segment operating income more than tripled to $4.8 billion, lifting ISG margin to 15.0% from 8.8%. Client Solutions revenue grew 20% to $15.0 billion. Vice chairman Jeff Clarke said Dell booked $60.9 billion in AI server orders and exited the quarter with a $95 billion backlog. Free cash flow fell 47% to $986 million, though Dell's adjusted measure rose 224% to $8.1 billion after adding back $6.7 billion of financing receivables.

Dell lifted full-year revenue to $192 billion from $167 billion, a 69% year-over-year increase, and took its AI-optimized server revenue outlook to $74 billion from $60 billion. Non-GAAP EPS guidance went to $25.50 from $17.90. Third quarter revenue is guided to $49 billion.

title: Dell's AI Server Backlog Reaches $95 Billion
